probes.text: Kim keeps watch on a leisurely round of golf while Jimmy slips unnoticed into the country club's locker room.
A long wordless sequence of a mansion being emptied, its white Cadillac rolled up onto a flatbed truck.
A souvenir tequila bottle stopper tumbles out of a cabinet as it is carried away with the furniture.
Jimmy turns up at a strip-mall tax preparation office run by a chirpy suburban husband and wife he knows.

fine_only.text: Gus and Bolsa stand over Hector at the nursing home, promising him they will avenge Lalo.

probes.text: Jimmy and Kim toy with the idea of buying a duplicate of Howard's car before settling on something simpler.
Nacho, his shot-up truck no longer drivable, is left to hole up out of sight until daylight.
Evicted from the back room of the nail salon, Jimmy scouts out a potential new office and shows it to Kim.
Jimmy finds his fellow lawyers now cold toward him, while local criminals keep turning up wanting him to represent them.
Jimmy, done up to pass as Howard, drives Howard's car and picks up a woman from a motel.
Jimmy brings his old receptionist back on staff, hiring her to run the front desk again.
Kim keeps glancing over her shoulder, still unsettled by the possibility that Lalo is out there.
A veterinarian shows Jimmy and Kim his thick encrypted notebook of criminal contacts, mentioning he is getting out of the business.
Cliff invites Kim to Santa Fe to meet foundation people who fund work like her pro bono defense practice.
A private investigator reports that the couple's days are dull and routine, apart from one recent cash withdrawal.

fine_only.text: Jimmy sits bound to a chair in his own living room while Lalo heads back out into the night.

probes.text: Out of his usual uniform, Gus sits at a wine bar talking with his favourite sommelier, then leaves early.
In the department store, Gene lingers over a loud, garish shirt on the rack, then walks away without buying it.
At a set time, Gene uses a payphone to make a long-arranged call to Francesca.
Gene works a bar, buying rounds for a well-off man drinking alone until he is thoroughly drunk.
Jeff, driving a drunk passenger home, keeps offering him a bottle of water from the front seat.
In a flashback, Kim runs into Jesse on the sidewalk outside Saul's office building.

fine_only.text: Kim's days now consist of a drab office job at a Florida company that manufactures sprinklers.

probes.text: In a flashback, Saul asks Mike what he most regrets; Mike answers, then dismisses Saul's own reply as shallow.
Saul and Walt trade answers about their biggest regrets while holed up together, and Walt scorns what Saul comes up with.
Jimmy cuts the conversation with his brother short, assuming the interest in his work is really criticism.
